candidate.answerReason: The reduced attendance is 81 students, requiring 162 cookies. Ten recipes make only 150 cookies, while eleven make 165.

methods.label: Find attendance, then count full recipes
methods.explanation:
A decrease of \(25\%\) leaves \(75\%\) of the original attendance, so the number of students attending is
\[
108\cdot0.75=81.
\]
At an average of two cookies per student, they need \(81\cdot2=162\) cookies. Each full recipe makes \(15\) cookies, and
\[
10\cdot15=150<162,\qquad 11\cdot15=165\ge162.
\]
Thus ten recipes fall short, while eleven provide enough. They should make \(\boxed{11}\) recipes, choice \(\text{E}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses percentages, multiplication, and comparisons of whole batches, all within AMC 8 arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale: The targets are finding the remaining percentage of attendance and selecting the least sufficient whole number of recipes. The ceiling concept appears through the comparison of ten and eleven batches; formal function notation is unnecessary. Percentage conversion and per-person and per-recipe quantity relationships support the method.
